item.title: People may not hear about drug operations, but we are doing it - ACP Vusonilawe
item.description: People may not hear about operations, but we are doing it. That is the message from Assistant Commissioner of Police Kasiano Vusonilawe on the Fiji Police Force's ongoing drug operations.
item.content:encoded:
People may not hear about operations, but we are doing it.

That is the message from Assistant Commissioner of Police Kasiano Vusonilawe on the Fiji Police Force's ongoing drug operations.

Vusonilawe says the the Force has not stopped carrying out drug operations but has changed its operational strategies as criminals and drug dealers continue to adapt.

Responding to questions from the media on the apparent decline in publicly announced drug raids, Vusonilawe says criminals, drug dealers and others who go against the law have their own strategies and plans to outmanoeuvre police operations.

He says that is why police also have their own strategies and cannot continue with one trend of operations.

INSERT: ACP on police operations 28th July

When questioned by fijiivllage News on joint operations with the Republic of Fiji Military Forces, Vusonilawe says there are certain cases where police and the military come together to work as a joint team.

He says they demarcate cases because there are cases of national interest and there are routine cases.

He adds that the joint team is not deployed every day.

The Assistant Commissioner also stressed that the Fiji Police Force cannot tackle the drug problem alone.

He says police need the assistance of the public by providing information and supporting law enforcement efforts.

He adds that people also need to become more security-conscious and not assume Fiji is the same as it was in previous years.

A journey shaped by resilience, compassion and a commitment to serving others takes centre stage on this week's fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, as Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran shares the experiences that have defined her life.

Kiran reflects on the lessons that shaped her values, and she opens up about issues close to her heart, including violence against women and children, drugs, HIV, peacebuilding, and the importance of creating opportunities for vulnerable communities.

item.title: Conjoined twins Di Cecea and Jesipeli leave for life-changing separation surgery
item.description: After spending the first 10 months of their lives joined together, conjoined twins Di Cecea and Jesipeli Kikau will leave Fiji for Saudi Arabia tomorrow, where they are set to undergo life-changing separation surgery. The twins were born at the CWM in Suva alongside their sister, Hossana , and have since captured the hearts of many Fijians with their remarkable journey.
item.content:encoded:
After spending the first 10 months of their lives joined together, conjoined twins Di Cecea and Jesipeli Kikau will leave Fiji for Saudi Arabia tomorrow, where they are set to undergo life-changing separation surgery.

The twins were born at the CWM in Suva alongside their sister, Hossana , and have since captured the hearts of many Fijians with their remarkable journey.

The family will travel to King Salman Hospital , where a team of specialist surgeons will carry out the multi-million-dollar operation, fully funded by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on humanitarian grounds.

The Saudi Government is covering the family's airfares, accommodation and all medical costs, while Fiji's Ministry of Health and Medical Services is providing a medical escort to accompany the family throughout their journey.

The support comes through the close bilateral relationship between Fiji and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, giving the family access to specialist care that would otherwise be beyond reach.

The Ministry of Health says for the Kikau family, tomorrow's flight marks more than an overseas medical trip—it is a journey filled with hope, courage and the possibility of a new beginning.

They say Di Cecea and Jesipeli prepare for one of the most complex surgeries in the world, many Fijians will be keeping the twins, their parents and little Hossana in their thoughts and prayers, hoping the sisters return home healthy and ready to begin the next chapter of their lives.

item.title: Overflowing rubbish sparks health fears among Cunningham residents
item.description: Residents of Cunningham are raising concerns over piles of rubbish left along the main road, claiming the Suva City Council has not collected the waste for several days. One concerned resident says the foul smell has become unbearable and is now posing a serious health risk to the community.
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Cunningham are raising concerns over piles of rubbish left along the main road, claiming the Suva City Council has not collected the waste for several days.

One concerned resident says the foul smell has become unbearable and is now posing a serious health risk to the community.

He says stray dogs have been scavenging through the rubbish and dragging waste into surrounding areas, worsening the situation.

The resident also claims the large yellow rubbish bin is overflowing and has not been emptied.

He adds that while many people living in nearby informal settlements do not pay city rates, residents should still take responsibility for maintaining civic pride and disposing of their rubbish properly.

The Suva City Council has acknowledged receiving complaints and told fijivillage News that it is working with its contractors to have the rubbish cleared today.

item.title: A man in his 20s dies after carrier crashes off Keiyasi Road
item.description: A man in his 20s has died after the carrier he was travelling in veered off Keiyasi Road in Navosa and went down a slope yesterday. Police say the man was travelling in a carrier with several other people when the accident occurred, adding that the identities of the victim, the driver and the other occupants are yet to be confirmed.
item.content:encoded:
A man in his 20s has died after the carrier he was travelling in veered off Keiyasi Road in Navosa and went down a slope yesterday.

Police say the man was travelling in a carrier with several other people when the accident occurred, adding that the identities of the victim, the driver and the other occupants are yet to be confirmed.

A passerby discovered the crash scene and rushed the injured person to Keiyasi Hospital, where they were pronounced dead on arrival.

Police are continuing their investigations into the matter.

30 people have died in road accidents so far this year, compared to 35 during the same period last year.

item.title: Wrecked vehicle removed from Nabua roadside after safety concerns raised
item.description: A wrecked vehicle that had been left blocking a lane after the Nabua Bus Stop and before the Shalimar Junction has now been removed. This restores normal traffic flow along the busy route.
item.content:encoded:
A wrecked vehicle that had been left blocking a lane after the Nabua Bus Stop and before the Shalimar Junction has now been removed.

This restores normal traffic flow along the busy route.

The damaged vehicle, which was involved in an accident on Friday, had remained at the site for several days, prompting concerns from drivers about the safety risk it posed, particularly at night.

A concerned citizen had earlier highlighted that the vehicle was blocking an entire lane and that there were no warning cones or signs in the area to alert drivers , increasing the risk of another accident and contributing to traffic congestion.

Drivers are still being reminded to remain alert and drive carefully at all times.
